defect_observations.observation: Holm's example is cited (pp.67-68), but the handbook gives only its own values 0.4412670349 (Bonferroni) and 0.5631999191 (Holm). The source prints 0.439 and 0.565 (held txt lines 312-322; PDF p.5 = p.68). The handbook neither records the printed values nor explains the difference; 0.439 matches the rounded quantile 2.58. This is a source-fidelity note, not a coverage gap.

Holm p.67 (txt 285-289) says that, except in trivial cases, the step-down test has a strictly larger probability of rejecting false hypotheses than classical Bonferroni. thm:p15-mt-domination says only that the inequalities need not be strict. It does not record the source's strictness claim or state its conditions.

The added pointer promises 'the exact thresholds in nt^2 at which the exponential bounds fall below the one-sided and two-sided Chebyshev values'. thm:p15-w02b-p15-063-chebyshev-comparison gives exact thresholds only for A_3 (x_*) and 2A_3 ([x_-,x_+]). For A_1 and A_2 it gives only the sufficient condition nt^2>x_* and the small-t reversal of part 3. The wording overstates what is proved. The owed C008 entry text itself is fully proved.

The text calls the general-filtration statement (adapted X_i with deterministic conditional means) 'the source's common-range extension'. Hoeffding p.18 (2.18) states the martingale condition only relative to the partial sums S'_1..S'_m. The handbook version generalises the source, and annex 306-319 proves it, but the text does not mark it as a generalisation.
